title: The Friday surah
hook: many read al-Kahf every Friday, a practice drawn from hadith (Hakim; Bayhaqi)
tomorrow: The young men in the cave

segments.voice: Yesterday: Fajr, the dawn recitation. Your line was dawn is witnessed. Today, a new surah.

A Friday morning, a mosque, an hour before the noon prayer. Along the walls, people sit alone, each with a Qur'an open to the same place. Ask one of them and you may hear: it's Friday, so it's al-Kahf. Surah eighteen, The Cave: a surah with a weekly appointment. Some read it in Arabic, some in translation, some under their breath. Today: where that appointment comes from.

The custom rests on a hadith recorded by al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi: whoever reads Surat al-Kahf on Friday, a light will shine for them between the two Fridays. Hadith scholars have discussed how strong its chains are, and the practice has lasted. Because the Islamic day begins at sunset, some read it on Thursday night, others on Friday itself. Another hadith, in Sahih Muslim, says that whoever memorizes the first ten verses of al-Kahf will be protected from the Dajjal, the great deceiver of the end of time. That's one reason some families teach those verses early. And Bukhari tells a scene: a companion was reciting al-Kahf at night, his horse tied nearby, when a cloud came down over him and began to circle, and the horse grew restless. In the morning he told the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, who said: that was the sakinah, the tranquility, which came down for the Qur'an. The surah opens, in Pickthall's words: "Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed therein any crookedness". Then come four long stories: young men who hide in a cave, a man with two gardens, Musa traveling to learn from a stranger, and a powerful traveler who builds a wall. Some teachers today read them as four trials: of faith, wealth, knowledge and power. That framing is a modern reading, not a hadith, but it helps hold the surah in your head. This week, one story at a time.

segments.voice: Think through your coming Friday and find a half hour that could belong to al-Kahf: before work, at lunch, after the noon prayer, on the train. If the whole surah feels like a lot, picture just the first ten verses, in Arabic or in translation, and where you'd sit to read them. If you pray, you can ask for that week of light.
Al-Kahf. The Cave, read each week by many Muslims for a light that lasts from one Friday to the next. Today's word.
Your line: friday's surah. A light from one Friday to the next. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Many Muslims read Surat al-Kahf every Friday, or from Thursday sunset, alone or in groups at the mosque; some also memorize its first ten verses, following the hadith in Sahih Muslim.

chat.says: Why do so many people at the mosque read the same surah on Fridays?
options: A hadith says whoever reads al-Kahf on Friday has light until the next Friday.
Because al-Kahf is the only surah allowed to be recited on Fridays.
Because the surah itself commands reading it every Friday morning.
